purpose: Isosorbide dinitrate is used to prevent and treat chest pain (angina) caused by heart disease. It helps reduce how often you get chest pain episodes and makes them less severe. It may also be used to treat heart failure in some patients.
how_it_works: This medicine relaxes and widens your blood vessels, making it easier for blood to flow through them. When your blood vessels are wider, your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood. This means your heart gets more oxygen, which helps prevent or relieve chest pain.
common_side_effects: Headache is very common, especially when you first start taking this medicine — it usually gets better over time. You may also feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when you stand up quickly. Flushing (feeling warm or red in the face), nausea, and low blood pressure can also occur.
warnings: Never take this medicine with erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), or vardenafil (Levitra) — this combination can cause a dangerous and life-threatening drop in blood pressure. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can trigger chest pain. You can build up a tolerance to this medicine, so your doctor may schedule 'nitrate-free' periods each day to keep it working properly.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for preventing chest pain is 5 to 20 mg taken by mouth 2 to 3 times a day. Your doctor will likely schedule doses with a gap of several hours overnight to prevent your body from getting used to the medicine too quickly. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses vary depending on your condition.
